case_studies.title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges
case_studies.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) offers an effective approach for large language models to access external knowledge. However, existing methods rely on dense similarity retrieval and face inherent limitations in handling structured constraints and multi-hop reasoning. Incorporating knowledge graphs partially alleviates these issues, but at the cost of semantic fragmentation, high maintenance overhead, and difficult incremental updates. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language models struggling with structured constraints and multi-hop reasoning by introducing SAG, a structured architecture for retrieval and agent systems. The authors built SAG to improve the way language models access external knowledge. The result is a more effective approach to retrieval-augmented generation, but it's not directly applicable to cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.abstract: Recent position papers argue that the classical aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty framework is insufficient for interactive large language model (LLM) agents and call for underspecification-aware, decomposed, and communicable uncertainty representations that can unlock new agent capabilities such as proactive clarification seeking and shared mental-model building. case_studies.title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents
case_studies.abstract: Context-heavy agents place unusual pressure on the key-value (KV) cache: long prefixes are reused across many short turns, while concurrency determines whether the serving system can keep GPUs utilized. We study 4-bit KV-cache compression for this setting, using TurboQuant-style rotation and codebook quantization as a quality anchor and vLLM FP8 KV caching as the deployment anchor. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of key-value cache pressure in context-heavy agents by building a 4-bit KV caching system, resulting in improved task quality, cache residency, and serving throughput. The system uses TurboQuant-style rotation and codebook quantization. This research may be relevant to IT engineers managing cloud infrastructure that supports AI or machine learning workloads.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for AI or machine learning workloads, here is what to do: review your key-value cache configuration, consider implementing 4-bit KV caching, and evaluate the impact on task quality and serving throughput. case_studies.title: Human-on-the-Loop Orchestration for AI-Assisted Legal Discovery
case_studies.abstract: Autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in electronic discovery (e-discovery), where compounding errors across multi-step reasoning chains can constitute legal malpractice. Unlike single-turn retrieval, agentic workflows operating over privileged document corpora exhibit a class of failure we term "trajectory collapse": an early misclassification silently propagates, rendering an entire privilege review invalid. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of autonomous Large Language Model agents making errors in electronic discovery, by proposing a structured taxonomy of agentic failures in legal information retrieval. The authors built a framework to identify and mitigate these errors, which can lead to legal malpractice. The result is a more reliable AI-assisted legal discovery process.

case_studies.title: Optimal Order of Multi-Agent and General Many-Body Systems
case_studies.abstract: This paper develops a general framework for analyzing multi-agent systems with feedback loops between agents actions and collective observations. The framework is built on two fundamental agent-level variables: power, which measures agent influence on collective outcomes, and response functions, which determine how agents react to observations. We derive how macroscopic properties, including total power, useful power, entropy, order, fragility, and mobility, emerge from these two variables of heterogeneous agents. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding complex systems with multiple agents and feedback loops, by building a framework to analyze these systems, and resulting in a better understanding of how macroscopic properties emerge from individual agent interactions. The framework helps to study the trade-off between growth and resilience in these systems. It does not directly affect IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: AgentFinVQA: A Deployable Multi-Agent Pipeline for Auditable Financial Chart QA
case_studies.abstract: Financial chart question answering in regulated settings demands more than accuracy: practitioners must know which answers to trust before acting on them, and many institutions cannot send client data to external model providers. Yet existing chart-QA agents are accuracy-focused and opaque, and most assume proprietary API access; to our knowledge, none combines auditability with on-premise deployability without significant accuracy compromise. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of trustworthy financial chart question answering in regulated settings by building AgentFinVQA, a multi-agent pipeline that provides auditable and on-premise deployable solutions. The result is a system that maintains accuracy while allowing institutions to keep client data secure. This is not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but may be relevant to financial institutions with specific chart QA needs.

case_studies.title: Multi-LCB: Extending LiveCodeBench to Multiple Programming Languages
case_studies.abstract: LiveCodeBench (LCB) has recently become a widely adopted benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) on code-generation tasks. By curating competitive programming problems, constantly adding fresh problems to the set, and filtering them by release dates, LCB provides contamination-aware evaluation and offers a holistic view of coding capability. However, LCB remains restricted to Python, leaving open the question of whether LLMs can generalize across the diverse programming languages required in real-world software engineering. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited programming language support in LiveCodeBench, a benchmark for evaluating large language models. The authors built Multi-LCB, an extension of LiveCodeBench that supports multiple programming languages. The result is a more comprehensive evaluation of language models' coding capabilities.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on evaluating large language models for code-generation tasks, rather than managing or optimizing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
case_studies.abstract: When large language models serve as evaluators in multi-agent systems, their systematic evaluation biases propagate through the agent network. We introduce Contagion Networks, a formal framework for measuring how evaluator biases spread across interacting LLM agents. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluator bias propagation in multi-agent large language models, introducing a framework called Contagion Networks to measure how biases spread between agents, and found consistent bias propagation in a controlled experiment. The researchers built a formal framework and tested it with three distinct evaluator bias profiles. The result shows that evaluator biases consistently propagate between agents, which may affect the reliability of language model-based systems.
